passage:
Every Thursday, a dog named Bobo visits the children's library. Children read books to him.
Bobo does not understand every word, but he listens quietly. He never laughs when a child reads slowly or makes mistakes.
A boy named Henry used to hate reading aloud. His voice shook in class. But with Bobo, he felt safe. He read one page, then two, then a whole story.
After several weeks, Henry volunteered to read in class. His classmates were surprised.
The librarian says Bobo is not a magic dog. He simply gives children a quiet listener. Sometimes people improve faster when they are not afraid of being judged.
